purpose: Define the Phase 5 foundation for evidence-based evacuation building qualification outputs. This rulebook separates official designation from non-official candidate suitability and prepares validation rules for later P5-B matching/routing work.
nonClaims: Official designation can only come from official evidence.
Literature/report criteria can support strong_candidate or weak_candidate, but cannot make a building official_confirmed.
Routing results are estimated prototype routes, not official evacuation routes.
Hazard context is not flood simulation.
evidencePriority: official evacuation shelter / disaster facility data
official hazard/disaster maps and administrative disaster documents
OSM / routing data as auxiliary evidence

statusTaxonomy.description: Official evidence directly identifies the facility/building and the PLATEAU building match is sufficiently unambiguous.
Official evidence likely identifies the building, but spatial matching, naming, source date, geometry, or metadata ambiguity requires manual review.
Non-official or derived evidence strongly suggests suitability under documented criteria; this is not an official designation claim.
Limited or partial evidence suggests possible suitability, with significant uncertainty.
Available evidence is insufficient to qualify or reject the building.
Evidence or rule checks indicate the building should not be treated as an evacuation building candidate.

confidenceLevels.description: Evidence and spatial matching are strong enough for automated use with low residual uncertainty.
Evidence is plausible but has match, metadata, route, or source limitations that should be visible to reviewers.
Evidence is weak, incomplete, conflicting, or based mainly on candidate inference.
Evidence is unavailable or insufficient to assign confidence.

manualReviewTriggers: shelter point not inside building footprint

ruleGroups.description: Determines whether a building can be officially confirmed based on official shelter, evacuation building, disaster facility, or administrative evidence.
exampleRules: If an official evacuation building source identifies a building and the PLATEAU match is unambiguous, qualificationStatus may be official_confirmed.
If official evidence identifies a facility but the building match is ambiguous, qualificationStatus should be official_confirmed_with_review.
If only literature/report or PLATEAU-derived evidence exists, qualificationStatus must not be official_confirmed.
warnings: Do not claim official designation without official source evidence.
Do not treat third-party summaries as official primary sources.
manualReviewTriggers: official source conflicts with another official source

ruleGroups.description: Plans how official or candidate facility evidence should be linked to PLATEAU building records.
exampleRules: A contains match is preferred when the source point lies inside a single building footprint.
A nearest match can be used only with matchDistanceMeters and manualReviewNeeded when the point is outside a footprint.
Unmatched records must not be official_confirmed unless later manual review provides an approved override.
warnings: PLATEAU geometry supports matching but does not prove official designation.
Metric distance must be calculated in an appropriate projected CRS in future implementation.
manualReviewTriggers: shelter point not inside building footprint

ruleGroups.description: Plans candidate checks for safe floors, available vertical evacuation height, and height-related warnings.
exampleRules: Official safe-floor fields can support official_confirmed or official_confirmed_with_review metadata when official designation also exists.
Literature/report height criteria can support strong_candidate or weak_candidate, not official_confirmed.
Missing safeFloor or height data should create warnings and manual review for candidates.
warnings: Hazard depth context does not equal flood simulation.
Height criteria must be tied to a documented hazard scenario before use.

ruleGroups.description: Plans how official hazard maps and disaster documents provide context for warnings and candidate screening.
exampleRules: Official hazard map overlap can add warnings or support safe-floor review.
Hazard context can downgrade confidence or require manual review when applicability to Chuo Ward is unclear.
Hazard context alone cannot make a building official_confirmed.
warnings: Hazard context is not flood simulation.
PDF or visual-only maps should not be treated as reproducible geometry without later controlled processing.

ruleGroups.description: Plans how prototype route availability, distance, and travel time support accessibility warnings.
exampleRules: Estimated route distance and travel time can add routeAvailability, nearestRouteDistanceMeters, and estimatedTravelTimeSeconds.
OSM-derived route estimates must be labeled as prototype estimates.
Route availability cannot confirm official evacuation route status.
warnings: Routing results are estimated prototype routes, not official evacuation routes.
OSM network completeness and pedestrian access tags require review.

ruleGroups.description: Plans how capacity, expected crowding, and missing occupancy evidence should affect warnings and confidence.
exampleRules: Official capacity fields should be preserved when available.
Missing capacity should not disqualify a building by itself, but should add warnings and manual review.
Crowding assumptions from literature can support warnings, not official designation.
warnings: Capacity values may use different definitions across sources.
Crowding estimates are scenario assumptions unless official source fields provide them.

ruleGroups.description: Plans handling of missing source metadata, conflicting evidence, unknown values, and disqualification cases.
exampleRules: Conflicting official evidence should produce manualReviewNeeded and may produce not_qualified when evidence shows the building is unsuitable.
Insufficient evidence should produce unknown, not a candidate claim.
Missing sourceUpdatedAt should be preserved as null and listed in warnings.
warnings: Do not fill missing official fields with inferred values.
Do not treat unknown as qualified.
